title: WPSS/1266/2008 of POORAN SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1266 of 2008
Pooran Singh and Others ....... Petitioners
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & others ......Respondents
Present:
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Sr. Advocate, assisted by Mr. Mukesh Kaparwan, Advocate
and Ms. Niti Rana, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Addl. C.S.C. for the State.
Aggrieved by the final selection list prepared by respondent
nos.1 to 4 for appointment to the post of Sub-Inspector, Police, the
petitioners are before this Court. Petitioners seek that the selection of
the respondent nos. 5 to 7 for the purpose of training for their
promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector be quashed and mandamus be
issued directing the respondents to rectify the impugned result.
2. Briefly stated, it is the case of the petitioners that at
the relevant time, they were working as Constable Police. They were
eligible for consideration for their promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector. The petitioners belong to Scheduled Tribes category. On
15.03.2007, the respondent no.3 issued a circular for selection to the
post of Sub-Inspector by giving details of the process for selection.
The petitioners appeared in the preliminary examination. They were
selected. They were also successful in physical test and in the mains
examination. They appeared in the interview and the result was

2
declared. The grievance of the petitioners is that the three candidates,
who were selected against post reserved for scheduled tribes had
obtained such higher marks, which entitled them to compete with the
general category candidates. Despite that, those reserved category
candidates were not appointed under general category and the
candidates who secured less marks than those three reserved category
candidates were given appointment under General category. These
three candidates who had, according to the petitioner, obtained less
marks than the reserved category candidates are respondent nos. 5 to 7.
It is the case of the petitioners that had the three reserved category
candidates, who had secured marks so as to compete with the general
category candidates, been appointed in non-reserved category, the
petitioners being next in the waiting list of the reserved category would
have got selection to the post of Sub-Inspector. Various government
orders have been referred to in the petition so as to bring home the
point that if a reserved category candidate comes in the merit, so that
he may compete with the general category candidate, then such
candidate should be considered and included in the general category.
With these and related averments, the final select list has been
challenged, particularly, the appointment of respondent nos.5 to 7 has
been challenged that they have been included in the list in defiance of
the rules applicable for reservation.
3. The State in its counter affidavit claims that the final
select list was lawfully made. It is the case of the State that final select

3
list was made according to merit and option of the candidates between
Civil Police Branch and Intelligence Bureau Branch. On the basis of
priority expressed by the candidates, they were selected and sent for
training. It is categorically case of the State that seven candidates
belonging to the reserved category were selected against reserved
category despite having obtained marks so as to compete in the general
category because otherwise they were not getting the post of their first
priority. Therefore, taking their priority option, they were selected.
Subsequently, the State has also brought on record a government order
dated 01.08.1996 by way of supplementary counter affidavit and it is
stated that due to omission, it could not have been filed alongwith the
counter affidavit.
4. Respondent nos. 5 to 7, in their counter affidavit, have
supported the State case. According to them, the entire selection
process was meant for two branches of the Police, namely Civil Police
Branch and Intelligence Bureau Branch, for which, options were
invited before interview from each of the candidates so that they may
be placed in the merit list according to criteria for selection namely (i)
the merit of the candidate and (ii) the option submitted by the
candidate. According to the respondent nos. 5 to 7, the stand taken by
the petitioners in the entire writ petition is patently erroneous and
misconceived because the selection has been made on the basis of
government order dated 01.08.1996, which provides that if a reserved
category candidate is selected, he must be placed in the seniority list

4
keeping in view the priority option exercised by him. If the meritorious
reserved category candidate finds his place amongst the general
category candidate as per his priority option, he shall be placed in
general category candidates, but, on the contrary, if the meritorious
reserved category candidate is not getting place amongst general
category as per his priority option, he shall be placed amongst the
reserved category candidate.
5. Respondent nos. 8 to 10 in their separate counter
affidavit also supported the claim of the State. Their counter affidavit
is, in fact, is inline to the counter affidavit as submitted by respondent
nos. 5 to 7. They have also impressed upon the priority option
exercised by the candidates as well the government order dated
01.08.1996 for making selection to the post.
6. The petitioners in their separate rejoinder affidavits to
the different counter affidavits, have questioned the weightage given to
the option exercised by the candidates in the selection process, on the
ground that selection on the basis of priority expressed by a candidate
cannot sustain in the eye of law. The option and desire and the priority
of a candidate is his own choice and it cannot prevail over a settled
principle of law.
7. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, and learned
State Counsel.

5
8. None appears on behalf of the respondent nos.5 to 7
and respondent nos.8 to 10 at the time of final argument.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that
the entire selection process was initiated on the basis of
communication dated 15.03.2007 of the respondent no.3, by which, the
whole selection process was revealed. Learned senior counsel would
submit that this communication dated 15.03.2007 at serial number 9
prescribes as to how to prepare the final merit list. According to it,
final merit list was to be prepared on the basis of marks obtained in the
written examination and in interview/personality test and the
assessment of character role/service record. It is argued that this
communication dated 15.03.2007 nowhere prescribes that option of
any candidate will have any bearing in preparation of the final
selection list. Any action de-hors to this communication dated
15.03.2007, according to learned senior counsel, would be bad in the
eye of law.
10. Learned senior counsel also raised the following
points in his argument;
(i) The government order dated 28.04.2005 and
25.03.1994 also prescribes the mode of placing a reserved
category candidate against general category, if such
reserved category candidate competes with general
category.

6
(ii) The respondent nos. 5 to 7 did get less marks than the
first three candidates selected against the category
reserved for scheduled tribe candidates.
(iii) It is well settled proposition of law that the reserved
category candidate can compete for non reserve post and
in the event of their appointment to the said post, their
number cannot be added and taken into consideration for
working out the percentage of reservation. Petitioners are
next in the waiting list prepared for scheduled tribe
category and if the first three candidates selected under
the scheduled tribe category are given appointment in the
general category, in that eventuality, the appointment of
respondent nos. 5 to 7 will have to be quashed and the
petitioners will get appointment in the category reserved
for scheduled tribe candidate.
(iv) The respondents committed gross error in taking into
account the option of the candidates for their appointment,
particularly in the Police department because the
communication dated 15.03.2007 by which the entire
selection process was initiated nowhere makes mention of
the option.
(v) Even otherwise, it is argued that such an option cannot
override the settled principle of law. The entire selection
process is faulty.

7
(vi) The Government order dated 01.08.1996 was not
referred to by the State while submitting their counter
affidavit and subsequently, it was submitted, but, this
government order dated 01.08.1996 will not have any
bearing in the matter because the process for selection by
way of promotion was initiated by the communicated
dated 15.03.2007 which does not speak of any option of
the candidate.
(vii) The Government Order dated 01.08.1996 does not
speak of selection. It merely speaks of allotment of the
post. The question of allotting the post arise only once
selection is made, therefore, it is argued that even if the
government order dated 01.08.1996 is looked into, it does
not enable the respondents to make selection on the basis
of the option of any candidate. At the most, once final list
is prepared, the options could have been seen while
allotting the particular wings of the Police department.
(viii) The Government Order dated 01.08.1996 is not
applicable to the instant selection process because it is
made applicable to upper subordinate services, which are
quite distinct.
11. In support of his contention, learned senior counsel for
the petitioner placed reliance on the principles of law, as laid down in
the case of R.K. Sabharwal and others Vs. State of Punjab and Others,

8
(1995) 2 SCC 745 and State of Bihar Vs. Kaushal Kishore Singh and
Others, (1998) 9 SCC 104.
12. In the case of R.K. Sabharwal and others (supra), the
Hon'ble Supreme Court, inter alia, held that "on the other hand, the
reserved category candidates can compete for the non-reserved
posts and in the event of their appointment to the said posts, their
number cannot be added and taken into consideration for working
out the percentage of reservation."
13. Before the observation made by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the case of Kaushal Kishore Singh (supra) are looked into, it
would be apt to just examine the facts of that case. In the case of
Kaushal Kishore Singh (supra), the Bihar State Selection Service
Board advertised 978 posts for appointment, but, subsequently, some
more posts were included. There were about 7 categories of posts.
Their pay-scales were different. The Board considered candidates for
various posts as per availability at the time and recommended
candidates strictly on the basis of pay-scale and academic qualification
of job requirements. The High Court in that case had proceeded on the
premise that no merit list was prepared and the candidates who had
aptitude for certain job or entitlement were required to be considered
for appointment. Holding that the selection and appointment of the
candidates was prepared without merit list and without calling for the
option, it was held arbitrary and violative of Article 14 of the

9
Constitution. This order of the Hon'ble High Court was not upset by
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kaushal Kishore Singh
(supra). What the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed in that case is as
hereunder;
5. ..........................................We do not find that the criteria laid
down by the High court is correct in law. Even if options were called for
and given, it is not mandatory for the Government to accept options of the
candidates and make appointment to the post. Asking for option of
candidates is only a discretionary matter and the Government is not bound
to select the candidates on the basis thereof. Under these circumstances, the
candidates who applied for, though opted for, have no acquired rights,
much less indefeasible and absolute right for selection or appointment to a
particular post. As stated earlier, the Government have to prescribe an
objective and rational method or manner of allotment of the candidates
selected to the Departments, depending upon their job necessity and
requirement. Since the objective and rational criteria was not followed, we
decline to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.
14. On the other hand, learned State Counsel would submit
that in fact, the petition itself is not maintainable. Learned counsel
referred to Annexure-7 to the writ petition, which is a list of the
selected candidates of reserved category, to argue that even the
petitioners have obtained marks less than those candidates who are
included in the list of the selected reserved candidates. At this moment
only, this Court may like to mention that it is not the case of the
petitioners that in the existing list of selected reserved category
candidates, they may find place. What is the case of the petitioners is

10
that the top three candidates selected against reserved category had
obtained higher marks to enable them to compete with the general
category candidate. Therefore, those three top candidates selected in
the reserved category should be adjusted against the general category
and since the petitioners were in the waiting list for the reserved
category candidates, they would find place in the select candidate list
for their promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector. At the cost of
repetition, it may be noted that it is further case of the petitioner that in
that eventuality, the respondent nos. 5 to 7 who have been appointed
against the general category candidates will have to go because they
had obtained less marks than the three candidates who are at the top of
the list of the selected candidate list for the reserved category.
15. Learned State Counsel would also refers to the
government order dated 01.08.1996. When the Court questioned, how
is it applicable, because it speaks of its application to the upper
subordinate service examination of the State of Uttar Pradesh. Learned
State Counsel much fairly submits that he sought instruction from the
department about the applicability of the government order dated
01.08.1996 (it is annexure-1 to the supplementary counter affidavit of
the State) but he did not get any satisfactory reply.
16. Today, during the course of argument, learned counsel for
the State has also placed before the Court a communication dated
20.10.2008 made from Police Headquarter, Dehradun. It is not on

11
record, but, it has been placed before the Court. Let it be kept on
record. It only writes in paragraph 2 that the final selection for the post
of Sub-Inspector is proposed to be made on the basis of options that
may be exercised by the candidates. Then the Court wanted to know,
whether this proposal was ever finalized because this communication
speaks of just proposal. To it also, there is no reply. In fact, learned
State Counsel referred to a communication dated 02.09.2021, which
was made by the Inspector General, Personnel, Uttarakhand to the
Chief Standing Counsel, Nainital on the subject. In paragraph 5 of this
communication it is written that the promotion was made for two
posts. But, where are the two posts because the communication dated
15.03.2017 speaks of promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector i.e. one
post. So the communication which is placed during the course of
argument today by the learned State Counsel does not help the State.
17. The question, which falls for consideration is within a
very narrow compass. Learned State Counsel admits the settled
position of law that if any reserved category candidate can compete for
non-reserved post, he will get his appointment in the non-reserved
category.
18. According to learned State Counsel, this has been done in
the present case also, but, what is being argued is that while making
selection, the option of the candidates were also considered. The
process was undertaken for selection by way of selection to the post of

12
Sub-Inspector, Police. Admittedly, there were two wings, Civil Police
and Intelligence Bureau. The promotion was not made for any branch.
It was not a case of isolated promotion of Sub-Inspector in Civil Police
or Sub-Inspector in Intelligence Bureau. The process was initiated for
promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector. The process was initiated on
the basis of communication dated 15.03.2007. This communication
dated 15.03.2007 has categorically laid down as to how the final list
shall be prepared. The basis of final list was to be prepared on the basis
of marks obtained in the three different stages by the candidate. They
are mains examination, interview/personality test and assessment of
character role/service record. This communication dated 15.03.2007
does not speak of any other method of assessing the efficiency of a
candidate. There is no reference to any option.
19. In their supplementary counter affidavit, State has made
reference to a government order dated 01.08.1996. The private
respondents who have filed different counter affidavits, though not
represented at the time of final argument, have also made reference to
government order dated 01.08.1996. It is annexure-1 to the
supplementary counter affidavit dated 08.09.2010 filed by the State. A
bare perusal of the subject of this government order dated 01.08.1996
reveals that, in fact, this government order relates to Combined
State/Upper Subordinate Service Competitive Examination,
particularly, allotment of the posts and ensuring reservation.
Admittedly, the process for selection in the instant case was not for

13
Upper Subordinate or Combined State Services. It is not the case of the
State that the promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector falls within the
ambit of Combined State/Upper Subordinate Service. So, how is this
government order dated 01.08.1996 applicable in the instant case? In
fact, apparently, it is not applicable to the process of selection in the
instant case.
20. Moreover, if this government order dated 01.08.1996 is
examined, it does not speak of selection on the basis of option. It
speaks of the allotment of the posts. It appears that under this
Combined State/Upper Subordinate Service, there are various posts,
for which a combined examination is conducted and based on the
selection list, the allotment is made as per the Government Order dated
01.08.1996. In the instant case, the process was initiated for selection
to the one post of Sub-Inspector. So this government order otherwise
also is not applicable in the instant case.
21. In the instant case, candidates had no choice, but, to get
appointment as Sub-Inspector. It is a different matter as to which wing
is allotted to them, Civil Police or Intelligence Bureau. For that
purpose, perhaps, once final list is prepared, the options would have
been taken into consideration by the respondent State. But, while
preparing final selection list for one single post, the options could not
have been a criteria alongwith the marks obtained in the written
examination, in the interview test/personality test or assessment of

14
character role/service record. Respondent State has done it. By
including the criteria of option exercised by the candidates while
making final selection list, a mistake in law has been committed. This
is not in accordance with the procedure. No government order, no
circular or even letter has been placed before this Court, which may
enable the State to consider the option of a candidate while preparing
the final selection list to one post namely Sub-Inspector.
22. Therefore, this Court is of the view that in the instant
case, an error has been committed. The final selection list is vitiated
and it deserves to be quashed with the directions to the respondent
State to make final selection list in view of the communication dated
15.03.2007, within a period of four months.
23. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed.
24. The final selection list prepared in the matter is quashed.
Respondent nos. 1 to 4 are directed to prepare final selection list as per
communication dated 15.03.2007 of the respondent no. 3, within a
period of four months.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 03.09.2021
Ujjwal
